summary: fix(sync): keep names the dependent pass owns out of the flat worker pool, and name the resource on the one silent error path (issue #14)
reason: `sync --resources journal_entries,bank_accounts` sets both `resources` (the flat worker pool's work list) and `parentFilter` (the dependent pass's filter), because a named parent is meant to cascade to its children. The flat pool therefore also ran every named dependent: syncResource emitted sync_start and then failed in syncResourcePath, whose map holds the only flat resource of this API (`companies`), and the early return handed back syncResult{Err} without emitting any event - unlike every later error path. The collector counted those failures and printed them only under --human-friendly, so a machine-mode run of two resources that both synced correctly through the dependent pass reported `resources: 4, success: 2, errored: 2` with no way to tell which two failed (the number recorded in docs/ACCEPTANCE.md). The exit policy never caught it: criticalResources is empty and there were successes, so the run exits 0. Fix, in two parts: the enqueue loop skips any name isDependentSyncResource() reports as owned by dependentResourceDefs(), so a named dependent runs exactly once, in the pass that can actually sync it (`--resources journal_entries` now reads resources: 1, success: 1, errored: 0); and the syncResourcePath error path emits syncErrorJSON(resource, "", err) before returning, so a name that is neither flat nor dependent surfaces by name in machine mode instead of as an anonymous count. Exit-code semantics are unchanged: an unknown name is still an error, and with no successes the run still exits non-zero. Naming the parent (`--resources companies`) still cascades to every dependent, which is what the cascade rule in the command's Long help promises. Review follow-up: the skip exposed a third silent path in the same command. With the flat pool no longer claiming the name, `sync --resources journal_entries --agent` against a mirror that holds no companies row printed `resources: 1, success: 1, errored: 0` and exited 0 — syncDependentResource found an empty parent table, printed a line only under --human-friendly and returned a bare syncResult, so machine mode could not tell 'nothing changed' from 'the mirror has no parents yet'. It now returns the warned result built by the hand-authored dependentParentEmptyResult, which emits {"event":"sync_warning","resource":...,"reason":"parent_table_empty","parent_table":...,"hint":"run fiken-cli sync --resources <parent> first"} and makes the summary read warned: 1. The exit-policy code is untouched; because that run now has no successes at all, the pre-existing 'nothing synced' rule (all-warned exits non-zero) applies to it, which is the honest answer for a run that could sync nothing. Second review follow-up, three findings around the same call site. (1) `if err != nil || len(parentRows) == 0 { if len(parentRows) == 0 { ...empty... } ...error... }` could never reach its error case: every error path of dependentParentRows returns nil rows, so a locked or corrupt mirror was reported as parent_table_empty with a hint to sync a companies table that may well be full. The error is now tested first and returned as an error result; only then the empty case. (2) the --company scope filters the parent rows AFTER the query (scopeParentRowsToCompany, PATCH(mirror-canonical-resource-name)), so `sync --company <typo>` against a fully hydrated mirror emptied a non-empty parent set and reported the same parent_table_empty. The two states need different repairs, so the row count is captured before the scope filter and a scoped-out run gets its own reason: {"event":"sync_warning","reason":"company_not_in_parent_table","resource":...,"parent_table":...,"company":...,"hint":"check the --company slug or run fiken-cli sync --resources <parent_table>"}, still a Warn, exit policy untouched. (3) the summary's all-warned message said "%d resource(s) skipped due to insufficient access", which was true when every warn came from isSyncAccessWarning and is not true for parent_table_empty or company_not_in_parent_table. Reworded minimally to "%d resource(s) skipped without error; see the sync_warning events for the reasons" — the events already carry the per-resource reason. Exit code unchanged.

validated_outcome: make check green (go vet ./..., go test ./..., scripts/check-boundaries.sh). Hand-authored tests in internal/cli/sync_named_dependents_test.go run the real sync command against an httptest Fiken with a temp HOME, a temp config.toml and a seeded one-company mirror, and assert on the sync_summary JSON line: --resources journal_entries gives resources 1 / success 1 / errored 0 with no sync_error and no flat sync_start for the dependent; --resources companies still gives one flat sync_start plus all ten dependents (resources 11, errored 0); --resources not_a_resource gives exactly one sync_error naming it, errored 1, resources 1, and a non-zero command error. Reverted-behaviour check: on the pre-patch code the first test reports `resources: 2, success: 1, errored: 1` for one requested resource and the third sees zero sync_error events. No live API call was made. Review follow-up run: make check green; go test -race ./internal/client/... ./internal/cli/... green. TestSync_DependentWithEmptyParentTableWarns drives the real sync command against a temp HOME whose mirror has NO companies row and asserts the parent_table_empty warning (resource, parent_table, hint) plus summary resources 1 / success 0 / warned 1 / errored 0 and the all-warned non-zero exit. Reverted-behaviour check: on the pre-patch branch the run reports success 1 / warned 0 and emits no warning. No live API call was made. Second review follow-up run: make check green; go test -race ./internal/client/... ./internal/cli/... green. TestSyncDependentResource_ParentQueryErrorIsAnError drives syncDependentResource against a closed store handle (the cheapest unreadable mirror) and asserts Err names the failed parent query, Warn is nil and no parent_table_empty event was emitted; pre-fix it returned the warning and no error. TestSync_CompanyNotInParentTableWarns runs the real command with --resources journal_entries --company nosuchco against a mirror holding one company and asserts the company_not_in_parent_table warning (resource, parent_table, company, hint), no parent_table_empty, summary resources 1 / success 0 / warned 1 / errored 0, and an all-warned exit whose message no longer claims insufficient access; pre-fix it warned parent_table_empty and exited with the access wording. No live API call was made.
